name: Read dog body language
blurb: Dogs communicate constantly and most people miss almost all of it. Learning the signals prevents bites, reduces stress, and makes you far better company for a dog.
gear: Dogs to watch — a park bench is a good classroom
A guide to canine calming signals
steps: Learn the early stress signals: lip licking, yawning out of context, turning the head away, a raised paw, whale eye showing the whites.
Learn that a wagging tail is arousal, not necessarily friendliness. Look at height, speed and stiffness.
Learn to read the whole dog together — a stiff body with a wagging tail is a warning, not an invitation.
Learn the escalation ladder, from subtle avoidance through growling to snapping, and understand that a growl is useful information.
Learn appropriate greetings: no looming over, no direct staring, let the dog approach you.
Practise by narrating what dogs are saying in a park before anything happens.
tips: Punishing a growl removes the warning without removing the feeling, which creates a dog that bites without warning.
Most bites to children happen after a long series of ignored signals. Learning them is genuinely protective.
proof: You can predict a dog is uncomfortable and intervene before it escalates, repeatedly.
